title: Create Target Array in the Given Order
statement:
You are given two integer arrays `nums` and `index` of the same length. Start with an empty array `target`. Then, for `i = 0, 1, 2, ...` in order, insert `nums[i]` into `target` so that it ends up at position `index[i]`; the elements already at that position and after it each move one place to the right.

Return `target` once every pair has been processed. Each `index[i]` is guaranteed to be a valid insertion position at the moment it is used.
notes:
## Intuition

The rules already describe an algorithm, so the job is to carry them out faithfully. Inserting into the middle of an array means opening a gap: every element from the insertion point onward slides one place right, starting from the end so nothing gets overwritten. With at most 100 elements, this direct simulation is plenty fast.

## Approach

1. Start with an empty `target`.
2. For each `i`, set `position` to `target.length`, the first free slot past the end.
3. While `position` is greater than `index[i]`, copy the element at `position - 1` into `position` and step left. This shifts the tail right by one.
4. Write `nums[i]` into the opened slot `index[i]`.
5. Return `target` after the last pair.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [0,1,2,3,4]`, `index = [0,1,2,2,1]`. The first three pairs append at the end: `[0]`, `[0,1]`, `[0,1,2]`. For `i = 3` the `2` slides from slot 2 to slot 3 and `3` goes into slot 2: `[0,1,3,2]`. For `i = 4` the elements at slots 3, 2 and 1 slide right in that order and `4` goes into slot 1: `[0,4,1,3,2]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): each insertion may shift every element already placed.
- Space: O(n) for `target`.

## Pitfalls

- Shift from the right end toward the insertion point; shifting left to right copies one value over all the others.
- Inserting at `index[i] = target.length` is valid and means appending; the loop then does nothing.
- Later insertions move earlier ones, so a value's final position is not `index[i]`; writing `target[index[i]] = nums[i]` without shifting gives the wrong array.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `target` | the array being built |
| `i` | which pair of `nums` and `index` is being inserted |
| `position` | the slot being filled while the tail shifts right |

narration.2: Begin with an empty target array.
narration.3: Process the pairs strictly from left to right.
narration.4: Start at the first free slot just past the end.
narration.5: Keep shifting until the gap reaches the requested position.
narration.6: Move the element on the left one place to the right.
narration.7: Step left to the next element that must move.
narration.9: The gap is now at index[i]; drop nums[i] into it.
narration.11: Every pair has been inserted, so target is complete.
